scope: Single-lane Astra holistic result; not an all-lane aggregate.

overall.note: final-report.md reports M1–M6/M8 green and two successful scale replays. Integrated authorization, sync, and media were strong fits; Quarry’s restricted shapes and documented work ceilings prevent an ideal score. Agent/environment correction costs are excluded.

setup_and_docs.note: diary.md M1 found the published password/profile path sufficient; M2 praised concrete scale and replication guidance. Guides supported later milestones. run-log.md attributes installation and watcher problems to agent/environment causes, with no established misleading documentation.

data_modeling.note: essay.md praises concise, unified schema, policy, aggregates, and scheduling, while describing restrictive program shapes and unfamiliar compiler vocabulary. diary.md M8 highlights subtle reference-driven index selection; the resulting implementation mistakes remain agent-attributed.

authorization.note: diary.md M3–M5 describes membership-scoped sync, send-time recipients, retained pre-removal history, and assets sharing row rules. M8 reused membership authority for digests; final-report.md records successful server-side revocation and expiry proofs.

queries_and_live.note: diary.md M1–M3 reports live updates and pagination without authored polling. M5 held offline search and M8 Trending worked; Global needed a separate event table, and queries required explicit bounds and carefully shaped merges.

writes_and_transactions.note: M3 arrival ordinals, M6 mutation identities and ordered settlement, and M8 durable markers/effect commit boundaries supported the required semantics (diary.md; essay.md). Both scale replays passed; run-log.md classifies incorrect write-ID encoding as agent-error.

offline_sync.note: essay.md describes platform-owned durable rows, media, and ordered mutations. final-report.md records cold-web queue/search persistence and M8 convergence proofs. Native runtime behavior remains unproven; composer races were agent errors, not sync defects.

media_assets.note: diary.md M4–M5 describes upload validation, row-governed access, and one-fetch columns without separate signing or revocation services. final-report.md records recipient playback, revoked-fetch refusal, cold ordinary-media retention, and consumed-once exclusion.

background_work.note: M5 client-free expiry and M8 scheduled digest restart, authorization, and deduplication proofs passed (final-report.md). Effects and Quarry backfills worked, but the report documents atomic per-recipient digest computation potentially parking at job bounds.

client_integration.note: M1 hooks and generated operations supported live clients; M6 documented token-only access worked, and every milestone produced Hermes output (diary.md; final-report.md). Cold web launch required an authored app-shell service worker; native lifecycle evidence stops at builds.

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: run-log.md records actionable principal-leading-index, prediction-eligibility, and exact write-ID diagnostics. M8 doctor inspection helped uncover attribution mistakes. final-report.md reports no demonstrated Snapback defect; frontend, harness, and environment correction loops are excluded.

scale_and_limits.note: final-report.md records 167,243 settled actions, 100,015 messages, and 1,002 conversations on the completed program, with modest measured query growth. These are builder diagnostics, not the full independent probe matrix; finite work ceilings remain relevant.

operations.note: M2/M3 idempotent seeds, M8 Quarry attribution backfill, doctor inspection, fresh replay stores, and digest restart recovery worked (diary.md; final-report.md). Operational evidence is local; the separate M7 migration exercise was intentionally not run.

snapback4.verdict: Snapback 4 was an excellent fit for this lane’s messenger, substantially reducing synchronization and media-policy plumbing while requiring precision within Quarry’s bounded programming model.
snapback4.would_use_again_for: I would use it again for private realtime applications needing durable offline writes and membership-controlled media, with workloads designed around the documented query and job ceilings.

comparison_notes: essay.md compares Snapback’s integrated authorization, assets, expiry, and offline queues favorably with the composition work the author expects in Supabase or a conventional server stack.

diary.md and essay.md contrast Quarry’s explicit bounds and local-execution eligibility with Convex’s familiar application-language functions, identifying a tradeoff between integrated guarantees and authoring flexibility.
essay.md acknowledges SQL tooling and ecosystem familiarity as reasons to prefer Supabase for other teams.
These are the lane author’s architectural comparisons, not measured competing builds or empirical comparisons with earlier Snapback releases.
